### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19c1c3f65f9e1e34fa43f7e50b2a4a190aee7fed` — the merge of head `6c7ff71e5e53ef2fc6f62ad391d033f6eda49d33` into base `f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19c1c3f65f9e1e34fa43f7e50b2a4a190aee7fed && git checkout 19c1c3f65f9e1e34fa43f7e50b2a4a190aee7fed
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420 6c7ff71e5e53ef2fc6f62ad391d033f6eda49d33 && git checkout -B drift-repro f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420 && git merge --no-ff 6c7ff71e5e53ef2fc6f62ad391d033f6eda49d33

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b6b340a3db9bf6254c5941f56c410bc3fe85e74b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/by-id-write-row-reread.posture.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/authz-matrix-gate.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/filter-subtree-provenance.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-lowering.ts, packages/spec/src/data/readable-ids.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`readUnlessRefused`, `callerCannotReadAddressedRow`, `copyOfCallerPredicate`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-check-stored-form.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`findOne`), packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts, packages/objectql/src/external-driver-floor.ts, packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts, packages/core/src/utils/readable-ids-driver-refusal.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-read-exit-fault.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (`declaredHttpStatus`)

Inputs read: PR #30307 body and file list, the net diff against `main` at the head above (7 files, +550/-19), the head's check-runs, and the cited code at the head. Check-runs as read at 2026-11-05 05:54 UTC: every concluded run is `success` or `skipped` (Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates and all Lint/Type Check lanes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards); `Test Core` shards 3, 5, 6, 7 `success`, shards 1, 2, 4, 8 still `in_progress`, so the required `Test Core` context had not concluded — not a pass yet.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Rule (1), step 2.7 — correct. The caller-context re-read's outcome is classified by `readUnlessRefused`, the classification the write doors already use (`callerCannotReadAddressedRow`, the predicate write's read question): a declared 4xx keeps the record-level `403` and skips the not-found question, one answer for a row and for no row; anything undeclared or 5xx propagates as raised, before anything is written. `declaredHttpStatus` reads `status`/`statusCode` in 400–599 only, so an undeclared store fault is never mistaken for a refusal.
2. Rule (2), step 2.7 and 2.8 — correct. The write predicates ride under one fresh `$and` node built at the call site and marked `'policy'`; a frozen or shared member cannot leave the node unmarked (the mark is first-mark-wins and no-ops on frozen input, so marking the fresh wrapper rather than the members is the right choice). `collectConditionFields` stops at a `'policy'` node and everything beneath it; an unmarked node, an `'author'` node, a spread copy, a JSON copy and a structured clone are judged (the mark is a non-enumerable symbol key; none of those carries it). The mark reaches the guard on the real engine: `findOne` spreads the query into its AST without rebuilding `where`, and the token/lowering rewrites copy a replaced node's mark onto its replacement (`filter-lowering.ts`).
3. Rule (3) — holds. A row the caller cannot read and an id naming no row still reach `callerCannotReadAddressedRow` and answer not-found as for every caller; a row the caller reads but may not write answers `403`; a caller the read door refuses answers `403` for every id; a system write is not the gate's; the predicate write's read question still copies and judges the caller's verbatim predicate. Pinned on a real engine under `group` and `isolated` with `single` as control (19 pins), plus the organization administrator's assignment removal.
4. No existence signal is added by rule (1): the re-read is asked for every id alike, and the propagated fault is the read door's own answer to this caller for a direct read of the same object, so the write door discloses nothing the read door does not.
5. The Layer 0 matrix helper now reads the platform subtree's members; every matrix expectation is unchanged — correct.
6. Public surface: `collectConditionFields` / `assertReadableQueryFields` are exported from `@objectstack/plugin-security`; their semantics widen (a marked platform subtree is no longer judged). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right declaration.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` — consistent. The widening is the admitted writes; the changed failure status is the write door following the contract the read door and `readUnlessRefused` already declare, not a narrowing of a published acceptance set, and the error the caller now receives is the one a direct read already gives it, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed. Level follows the kind: `none` ⇒ `patch`. The changeset's wording must change (③ must-fix below); its declarations and level stay.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Must-fix — public text below rule level.** The order's disclosure rule (security-findings §6: title, body and changeset carry the hardening rule only) is breached in three places: the changeset's two sentences that state what the doors answered before this change; the body's 维护者速读 second bullet (为什么改); and the ablations block, which narrates the doors' answers with each rule removed. Each must be reduced to the rule form (the "now holds" sentences already present are at rule level and suffice); the ablations block may keep pin counts only. The changeset ships in CHANGELOG, so it is the first to fix. This is a FAIL.
- Open question in the body (step 2.8's catch-all): answered below under ④; it is a ruling request for the seat, not a change for this PR.
- Acceptance note on #30248: verified — `d0da8802a0` is on `origin/main` and merged into the branch at `f3d93267d6`.
- Prose checked true of the tree: the mark is the one step 3 already stamps on every injected read scope; no second guard and no second read; the mark does not survive a copy, a serialization or the wire; `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` maps to 503 at the transports; 19 pins in the new file; the predicate write's read question judges the caller's verbatim predicate.
- **Should-fix — rule (2)'s declared reach is narrower than its real reach.** The guard's skip applies to every `'policy'`-marked subtree that reaches step 2.9 inside a caller-context read's `where`, and the tree already marks such subtrees outside the two doors this PR names: the analytics read-scope merge (`withReadScope` and its FK expand hand a marked scope to `aggregate` under the caller's context) and a sibling middleware's sharing scope when it composes before this one. All are platform predicates — the rule's own direction, nothing of the caller's is admitted — but the changeset and body should name the reach, and a pin on the analytics face is owed (a follow-up card is acceptable).
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note.

### ④ Design judgment

- `predicate-guard.ts`: the skip is node-level and fail-closed — `null` and `'author'` are judged, only a positive `'policy'` is skipped — so the tree's "unmarked ⇒ caller's" direction holds. Attempts to break rule (2) from the wire fail by construction: JSON carries no symbol key; a spread copies enumerable keys only; `structuredClone` drops symbols; a caller's `$and`/`$or` wrapping arrives unmarked and is judged; first-mark-wins prevents a later boundary re-vouching a policy node as the caller's. The platform never copies a caller-authored predicate into a marked subtree: every rewrite (`filter-lowering`, `filter-comparand-shape`, `rls-compiler`, `rls-check-stored-form`, `readable-ids-driver-refusal`) copies the replaced node's own mark, so a caller node yields an unmarked or `'author'` rewrite; the sharing, RLS and analytics scopes are built from policy and shares, never from the caller's `where`; the predicate write's read-door scope is an id list; view filters arrive over the wire unmarked. In-process code running under the caller's context (a hook, a plugin) can import the mark, but that code can equally set a system context — not a boundary this guard draws. Holds.
- `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` (step 2.7): the fresh wrapper is the right place for the mark. Step 3's vouch on the re-read is unchanged (the root `where` keeps its identity, so it is still vouched as the caller's), and the inner `'policy'` node now wins positionally inside it, which also decides what a driver-side refusal raised from inside the platform's predicates may name — the direction is withholding, a tightening the PR does not claim; mechanism in the reviewer's note. The store-fault propagation adds no per-id answer (① 4). Holds.
- `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts` (step 2.8): the mark holds as at 2.7. The catch-all stays by the recorded ruling the comment names and is consistent with rule (3) as the seat set it; after this PR it differs from step 2.7 for a store fault only, so a detail write under an unreachable store is answered as a denial where the master's own door would now raise the fault. That asymmetry needs a ruling, not a code change here — the seat should put it to the maintainer; recorded here as should-fix.
- Tests: the posture file pins both rules and the rule (3) invariants on a real engine with the real plugin, including the row/no-row equality under a declared refusal and the equality of the hidden-column caller's answers with the plain caller's; the unit pins cover the copies. The analytics reach (③ should-fix) is unpinned.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8a92cab832364dd012598c177421646d878026d6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/authz-matrix-gate.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/by-id-write-row-reread.posture.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.test.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-platform-scope-predicate-guard.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/filter-subtree-provenance.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-lowering.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`readUnlessRefused`, `callerCannotReadAddressedRow`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/record-row-write-probe.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`findOne`), packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts, packages/objectql/src/external-driver-floor.ts, packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts, packages/core/src/utils/readable-ids-driver-refusal.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (`declaredHttpStatus`), packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/read-audit.ts (`extractDetailReadId`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sys-user-self-service-route.test.ts; prose, checked sentence by sentence in ③: .changeset/by-id-write-row-reread-rules.md

Inputs read: PR #30307's body, its three comments (the docs-drift advisory 6650741217, the prior `## Contract review` on `b6b340a3db` with its FAIL, comment 6650951607, and the claim 6656180832), its file list (8 files, +703/−19), the net diff of the head against `main` (merge-base `09720e2c8a`; the head is a merge of `main` on top of `cc1fbac302`), the six commit messages, and the cited code read in the head tree. Check-runs on the head, read at about 10:56, 11:03 and 11:09 UTC. First read: every concluded run `success` or `skipped`; `Test Core` (8 shards), `Build Core`, `Live E2E UI` and the lint and type-check lanes in progress. Last read: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards` and every lint and type-check lane `success`; `Test Core` shards 2, 5, 6, 7 `success`, shards 1, 3, 4 still in progress, and **`Test Core (8/8)` `failure` at 11:07:38Z** — its annotation names the `plugin-auth` package's test command exiting 1, and its log names the same three pins as before. So the required `Test Core` context is red on this head, not a pass. On both prior heads (`b6b340a3db`, `cc1fbac302`) `Test Core (8/8)` concluded red on the same three pins of `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sys-user-self-service-route.test.ts`, each on the re-read's `where` shape this PR changes (④ must-fix); that file is untouched by the PR and by `main` since, and the red recurred on this head as expected. The dev's reported readings never include the `plugin-auth` suite.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept set, by-id update and delete (step 2.7) — right. Under `group` and `isolated`, a caller whose field rules hide a column the platform's write predicates name (the tenancy wall, a row-level write predicate) and who reads the addressed row is admitted; a row the caller cannot read and an id naming no row answer `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` as for every caller; a row the caller reads but may not write keeps `403`; a system write is not the gate's. Pinned on a real engine (19 pins), plus the organization administrator's in-boundary assignment removal on both assignment tables.
2. Accept set, controlled-by-parent detail write (step 2.8) — right. The same caller writes a detail under a master of its organization; a master of another organization answers it as it answers a caller who reads the column; nothing is written. Pinned.
3. Accept set, an aggregate under the caller's context — right. The read scope the analytics merge (`withReadScope`, its foreign-key expand) hands to `aggregate` is the platform's and is not judged; the caller's own filter on the hidden column is still refused `403`. Pinned on the real stack under `group` and `isolated`.
4. Reach — right as declared. A record-sharing read scope composed before this middleware is in the same class (its three production sites mark it the same way). The engine's own `ReadableIds` scope is marked the same way at its composer but is composed at the executor boundary, inside the middleware terminal, so it never reaches step 2.9 — consistent with the changeset's "every such subtree that reaches the guard".
5. Store fault on the re-read — right, and no new per-id answer. The re-read is asked for every id alike, the fault is the store's and not the row's, and the propagated answer is the read door's own to the same caller; a declared 4xx keeps the one `403` for a row and for no row (pinned equal). `declaredHttpStatus` reads `status`/`statusCode` in 400–599 only, so an undeclared fault is never read as a refusal; `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` declares no status and the transports answer it `503`.
6. Public surface — right. `collectConditionFields`, `collectQueryFields` and `assertReadableQueryFields` are exported by `@objectstack/plugin-security` and their semantics widen (a subtree marked as the platform's is not judged); `readUnlessRefused` is a module export the package index does not re-export. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right declaration.
7. The re-read's `where` shape at the engine — wrong, as incomplete. The write predicates now ride as one nested `$and` beside `{ id }` instead of spread beside it. Every fake engine a test composes the real middleware over observes that shape; the PR updated one consumer (`authz-matrix-gate.test.ts`) and missed `plugin-auth`'s `sys-user-self-service-route.test.ts`, whose three pins assert the shape verbatim by design and are red (④ must-fix). The production readers of the shape hold: `extractDetailReadId` walks the whole `$and` closure; `isRowWriteProbe` reads a symbol on the operation, not the filter.
8. Unclaimed tightening, withholding direction — right. With the platform's predicates under a node marked as its own, a refusal raised from inside them on the re-read is withheld (innermost mark wins, where before the unmarked parts took the root's author vouch), and the external-driver floor's "is this `where` the caller's own" answers no for the re-read. Both withhold more, never less.
9. Rule (3) unchanged, read in the tree: the predicate write's read question still copies and judges the caller's verbatim predicate (a copy carries no mark, so it is judged); step 2.9 still judges a write's `options.where` and a read's `ast.where`; step 3's vouch is unchanged; the delegated-write compositions are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` — consistent with the diff: no authorable key moves, the accept set only widens, and the changed status on a store fault is the write door following the classification the read door and the predicate door already declare, not a narrowing of a published accept set. Level follows the kind: `none` ⇒ `patch`. The changeset, sentence by sentence against the diff: the re-read under the caller's context with the platform's write predicates (step 2.7, whenever at least one write part is composed) — true; the second rule holding for the master read as well — true; a store fault propagating, `503` for `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, nothing written, only a declared 4xx keeping the record-level `403` — true; the master read keeping its `403` for every failure — true; the guard judging only the caller's predicate and not a subtree the platform composed and marked — true; the four named reach sites — true (④); "only platform-composed predicates are exempt; nothing the caller writes is" — true by the mark's fail direction; the `group`/`isolated` admissions and the other-organization/no-record equality — pinned; the unchanged list — true. All at rule level. The prior record's wording must-fix is resolved: `cc1fbac302` removed every sentence that narrated an earlier answer. The changeset is silent on the re-read's shape change, rightly: it is internal, not a published contract.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Prior FAIL's must-fix (public text below rule level) — resolved on this head: the changeset states rules only; the body's 为什么改 bullet states the rules; the ablations block carries pin counts only; test names and commit messages are rules. The title, body, commits, changeset and test names of this head stay at rule level — each says what a door holds or answers, none how it could be made to misbehave.
- Prior should-fix (rule 2's declared reach narrower than its real reach) — resolved: the changeset and body name the four reach sites, and a REST-level pin covers the analytics face.
- Open question in the body (step 2.8 keeps its catch-all `403`; "whether it should follow step 2.7 is left to the seat") — escalated, not resolved here. After this PR the two doors differ for a store fault only: a detail write under an unreachable store is answered as a denial on the master read, where the master's own by-id write raises the fault. The site's comment cites the ruling it follows, so changing it is a ruling, not a code change for this PR. Should-fix: the seat puts it to the maintainer.
- Acceptance note on #30248 — verified: `d0da8802a0` is in the head's history.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; head repo is the base repo (not a fork); draft; no governed path in the file list (Governed Surface Queue Guard green); 722 changed lines, under the 3,000 ceiling.
- Must-fix, the body's Verification: it reports every dispatch gate `0` and the `plugin-security` suite green, and nothing of `Test Core`, while `Test Core (8/8)` was red on both prior heads for this PR's own change. Once the pins are updated (④), the body names the `plugin-auth` suite's reading on the final head.
- Docs-drift advisory (`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` names `registerAuthzMiddleware`) — read; the page states no answer this diff changes. No action.

### ④ Design judgment

- `predicate-guard.ts` — holds. The skip is node-level and fail-closed: only a positive mark of the platform's own on the node itself is skipped; no mark and the author mark are judged. Tried to break it: a request cannot carry the mark in (it is not a visible key; a copy, a spread, a serialization and the wire drop it — pinned for the unmarked, author, spread and JSON cases); a caller's own `$and`/`$or` wrapping arrives unmarked and is judged; first-mark-wins means a later boundary cannot re-vouch a platform node as the caller's; every in-tree composer that marks a subtree as the platform's (step 3's injected scopes, the sharing middleware's three sites, the analytics merge and its FK expand, the engine's `ReadableIds` scope, now steps 2.7 and 2.8) marks a scope built from policy, shares or compiled RLS and vouches the caller's `where` separately, never wrapping caller input; every rewrite that replaces a node (`filter-lowering`, `filter-comparand-shape`, `rls-compiler`, `readable-ids-driver-refusal`) carries the replaced node's own mark, so a caller node never gains the platform's mark by rewriting. The ordering contract (the guard before this middleware's own injection) is unchanged.
